course.title: Tailoring and Fashion Design
course.tagline: Cut, sew and finish clothes that fit beautifully, from measurements to a finished outfit.

days.title: Your Tools and Workspace
days.goal: Set up a sewing workspace and identify every basic tailoring tool.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Clear a flat table at least 1m wide and set your machine on the left, iron on the right.
Lay out scissors, tape measure, pins, chalk, seam ripper and hand needles and name each one.
Thread your machine once slowly, following the numbered thread path in its manual.
Sew three straight lines on scrap cotton and check the stitch length.
days.task: Photograph your set-up workspace with every tool labelled on paper.
days.challenge: Sew a perfectly straight 30cm seam without the fabric drifting.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do before threading a sewing machine?
options: Raise the presser foot and follow the thread path
quiz.explain: Raising the presser foot opens the tension discs so the thread seats correctly.

quiz.q: Which tool is used to remove stitches?
quiz.explain: A seam ripper has a sharp point and blade made for cutting stitches without tearing fabric.

quiz.q: Why do you press seams as you sew?
options: It sets the stitches and gives a professional finish
quiz.explain: Pressing as you go sets stitches flat and keeps the garment shaping correctly.

days.title: Know Your Fabrics
days.goal: Tell cotton, Ankara, linen, chiffon and denim apart by look and feel.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Collect five small fabric swatches from a market or old clothes.
Hold each up to the light and note which are sheer, stiff or stretchy.
Pull each swatch gently both ways to test stretch and to see which way the threads run (this is called the grain).
Write the name, feel and best use of each swatch on a card.
days.task: Label five swatches with fabric name and one garment each suits.
days.challenge: Identify an unknown fabric from a friend's wardrobe by feel alone.

days.title: Take Accurate Body Measurements
days.goal: Measure bust, waist, hip, shoulder and length correctly on a real person.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Tie a ribbon around the natural waist so you can find it every time.
Measure bust, waist and hips snugly, keeping the tape level all round.
Record shoulder width, back length and sleeve length on a measurement sheet.
Repeat every measurement once and keep the second reading if it differs.
days.task: Complete a full measurement sheet for yourself or a willing model.
days.challenge: Measure someone in under five minutes with no errors on re-check.

days.title: Pattern Paper and Marking Tools
days.goal: Prepare pattern paper and mark grainlines, notches and seam allowances correctly.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Tape brown paper or newspaper sheets together into a 1m by 1m drafting surface.
Draw a straight arrow to show the grain (the direction the threads run) and a 90-degree cross line with a set square.
Mark 1.5cm of extra fabric for the seam (called the seam allowance) around a rectangle and cut it out cleanly.
Label the piece with its name, size, grainline and number of pieces to cut.
days.task: Draft and label one marked pattern piece with grainline and seam allowance.
days.challenge: Draw a perfect right angle and parallel grainline freehand with a ruler.

quiz.q: What is a grainline on a pattern piece?
options: An arrow showing the direction of the fabric grain
quiz.explain: The grainline arrow must run parallel to the selvedge so the garment hangs correctly.

quiz.q: What is pattern draping?
options: Shaping fabric directly on a dress form
quiz.explain: Draping shapes muslin on a form to create a pattern from the body itself.

quiz.q: Why add ease to a pattern block?
options: So the garment allows movement and breathing
quiz.explain: Ease is the extra room beyond body measurements that lets a garment move comfortably.

days.title: Draft a Straight Skirt Block
days.goal: Draft a basic straight skirt pattern (called a block) from real waist and hip measurements.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Divide your hip measurement by four and add 1cm of extra room (this extra room is called ease) for the quarter block.
Draw the waist, hip and hem lines on pattern paper using your measurements.
Shape the side seam with a gentle curve from hip to waist.
Add darts at the back waist, 1.5cm wide and 10cm long.
days.task: Finish a labelled straight skirt block on paper, ready to cut.
days.challenge: Draft the same block from a friend's measurements without help.

days.title: Reading a Commercial Pattern
days.goal: Read a shop-bought pattern envelope and cut the right size and pieces.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Find the size chart on a pattern envelope and match it to your measurements.
Identify the cutting layout diagram for your fabric width.
Trace one pattern piece, transferring all notches and dots.
Check the finished garment measurements printed on the tissue.
days.task: Trace and label one full pattern piece from a commercial pattern.
days.challenge: Explain what every symbol on a pattern piece means to a friend.

days.title: Project: Sew a Simple Straight Skirt
days.goal: Cut and sew a wearable straight skirt from your own block.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Pin your skirt block to fabric, matching the grainline to the fabric grain.
Cut both front and back pieces plus a waistband, adding seam allowances.
Sew the side seams, insert the zip, then attach the waistband.
Hem the skirt evenly and press every seam flat.
days.task: Finish a straight skirt you can try on and wear.
days.challenge: Sew the skirt with no visible puckering at the waistband.

quiz.q: Which measurement divides by four for a quarter bodice block?
quiz.explain: The bodice is drafted in quarters, so bust, waist and hip are each divided by four.

quiz.q: What is a dart for?
options: Shaping flat fabric to fit curves of the body
quiz.explain: Darts take in fullness so flat fabric follows the bust, waist and hip curves.

quiz.q: Where do you measure the natural waist?
options: At the narrowest point of the torso
quiz.explain: The natural waist is the narrowest point, usually a couple of centimetres above the navel.

project.title: Sew a Simple Straight Skirt
project.brief: Cut and sew a straight skirt from your own drafted block, with a zip and waistband.
checks: Cut on grain with seam allowances

days.title: Machine Basics: Threading and Tension
days.goal: Thread any sewing machine correctly and fix skipped or loopy stitches.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Re-thread the top thread and bobbin from scratch, step by step.
Sew a test line and inspect top and bottom for loops or tight puckers.
Adjust the tension dial one number at a time until both sides look even.
Clean lint from the bobbin area with a small brush.
days.task: Produce a test strip with balanced stitches on top and underneath.
days.challenge: Diagnose and fix a looping stitch problem in under five minutes.

days.title: Seam Finishes That Last
days.goal: Sew plain, French and overlocked-style seams that do not fray.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Sew a plain seam on cotton and press it open.
Sew the same seam as a French seam, which folds the cut (raw) edges inside so they cannot fray.
Finish a raw edge with a zigzag stitch close to the edge.
Compare all three seams after a firm tug and note which frays least.
days.task: Make a 15cm sample of each seam finish, labelled.
days.challenge: Sew a French seam on chiffon without the fabric slipping.

days.title: Cutting Fabric Accurately
days.goal: Lay out, pin and cut fabric on grain with clean, accurate edges.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Fold the fabric so the finished edges (called selvedges) meet and the grain runs straight.
Pin pattern pieces with the grain arrow running the same way as the finished edge of the fabric (the selvedge).
Cut with long smooth strokes, keeping the scissors flat on the table.
Mark all notches with small snips and darts with chalk.
days.task: Cut a full skirt front and back accurately on grain.
days.challenge: Cut a slippery fabric without it shifting off the line.

quiz.q: What does "cut on grain" mean?
options: Cut with the grainline arrow parallel to the selvedge
quiz.explain: Cutting on grain keeps the garment hanging straight instead of twisting.

quiz.q: Why mark notches on cut pieces?
options: To match pieces correctly when sewing
quiz.explain: Notches are alignment marks that show which edges join and where.

quiz.q: What is a seam allowance?
options: The fabric left between the stitching line and the cut edge
quiz.explain: Seam allowance, usually 1.5cm, is the fabric between the stitch line and the raw edge.

days.title: Darts, Gathers and Pleats
days.goal: Shape flat fabric to the body with darts, gathers and knife pleats.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Mark a waist dart on fabric and sew it from the wide end to a point.
Press the dart toward the centre back and check it lies flat.
Gather a 30cm strip by sewing two rows of long stitches and pulling the threads.
Fold and press three even knife pleats on a practice strip.
days.task: Make a sample strip showing one dart, one gather and one pleat.
days.challenge: Sew a dart that ends in a smooth point with no pucker.

days.title: Necklines: Round, V and Square
days.goal: Cut and finish three neckline shapes cleanly with facings.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Draw round, V and square necklines on paper and compare their depth.
Cut a facing (a shaped piece of fabric that finishes the neckline edge) for a round neckline and sew it right sides together.
Clip the curves, turn the facing inside and press it flat.
Topstitch 3mm from the edge to hold the facing in place.
days.task: Finish one round neckline with a facing that sits flat.
days.challenge: Cut a V-neck that meets in a sharp, clean point.

days.title: Sleeves: The Set-In Sleeve
days.goal: Set a sleeve into an armhole without puckers or twisting.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Measure the armhole curve and compare it with the curved top of the sleeve (called the sleeve cap).
Ease the sleeve cap with two rows of gathering stitches.
Pin the sleeve to the armhole, matching notches and the shoulder mark.
Sew slowly, easing the fullness in as you go, then press.
days.task: Set one sleeve into a practice bodice smoothly.
days.challenge: Set a sleeve with zero puckers on the first try.

quiz.q: How do you make a dress with no paper pattern?
options: Cut rectangles from your body measurements and sew them together
quiz.explain: Rectangles cut to your measurements can become a dress without a paper pattern.

quiz.q: What does elastic do in a rectangle dress?
options: It pulls the waist in so the dress fits without a zip
quiz.explain: Elastic in a casing gathers the waist to your size, so no zip or shaping is needed.

quiz.q: Why add extra fabric for seams and hems when you cut rectangles?
options: So the finished dress is the right size after sewing
quiz.explain: Seam and hem allowances are used up in sewing, so you must add them when you cut.

days.title: Project: Sew a Fitted Bodice Top
days.goal: Make a fitted bodice top with darts, a neckline facing and a zip.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Cut the bodice front, back and facing from your drafted block.
Sew the darts, shoulder and side seams, then press them.
Attach the facing and insert an invisible zip at the back.
Hem the bottom evenly and try the top on for fit.
days.task: Finish a fitted bodice top that fits at bust, waist and shoulders.
days.challenge: Fit the top on a model and fix one fit issue on the spot.

days.title: Zips: Invisible and Lapped
days.goal: Insert an invisible zip and a lapped zip neatly.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Press the seam where the zip will go and mark the zip length.
Pin the invisible zip face down on one side and stitch with a zipper foot.
Repeat on the other side and close the seam below the zip.
Insert a lapped zip on a practice piece, overlapping one side by 3mm.

days.challenge: Insert a zip in under 15 minutes with no wavy fabric.

days.title: Buttons, Buttonholes and Hooks
days.goal: Sew strong buttons, machine buttonholes and hook-and-eye closures.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: Mark button positions evenly on a shirt front, starting below the bust.
Sew a button with a thread shank so it sits above the fabric.
Make a machine buttonhole on scrap, then cut it open carefully.
Sew a hook and eye so the edges meet exactly without gaping.
days.task: Make a placket sample with two buttons and two buttonholes.
days.challenge: Sew a buttonhole on thick fabric without the machine jamming.

quiz.q: Why sew hand stitches the same length as machine stitches?
options: So hand sewing looks even and strong like machine sewing
quiz.explain: Even, regular hand stitches are both stronger and neater.

quiz.q: What is a backstitch used for?
quiz.explain: Backstitch overlaps each stitch, making it the strongest hand stitch for seams.

quiz.q: When should you use a thimble?
options: Whenever pushing a needle through fabric to protect your finger
quiz.explain: A thimble protects the middle finger and gives power to push the needle through.

days.title: Dress Construction Order
days.goal: Plan the correct order for building a dress from pieces to finish.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: List every step of making a simple dress, from cutting to hemming.
Sew darts and seams first, then join the bodice to the skirt.
Insert the zip before attaching the neckline facing.
Leave hemming and pressing until the very end.
days.task: Write a step-by-step build order for a dress and follow it on paper.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: Cut the lining pieces slightly smaller than the shell pieces.
Sew the lining bodice together exactly like the outer bodice.
Join lining and shell at the neckline, right sides together.
Turn, press and hand-stitch the lining to the zip tapes.
days.task: Line a practice bodice with no lining showing at the neckline.

video.title: 2 DRESSES IN 1 VIDEO! Easy Patternless Girls' Dress Sewing Tutorial

days.challenge: Style a full outfit for a client from measurements alone.

quiz.q: What is a patternless dress?
options: A dress cut directly from body measurements without a paper pattern
A dress made from one piece of fabric
quiz.explain: Patternless cutting drafts the shape straight onto the fabric using measurements.

quiz.q: Why cut two dresses in one video lesson?
options: To show the method works for different sizes and styles
quiz.explain: Repeating the method on a second dress proves the technique, not the luck.

quiz.q: What should you check before cutting a dress without a pattern?
options: Measurements, grain and enough fabric for both pieces
quiz.explain: Without a pattern there is no second chance, so measurements and fabric must be checked first.

project.brief: Build a full dress: bodice, skirt, zip, facing and hem, pressed and wearable.

days.title: Sew with the Simple Turn-Through Method
days.goal: Make a neat flat item using the simple sew-turn-topstitch method.

video.title: One Simple Technique = Countless Easy Sewing Projects | Beginner Friendly

steps: Place two pieces of fabric right sides together and pin them.
Sew all round the edge, leaving a 10cm gap on one side.
Turn the piece right side out through the gap and poke the corners out gently.
Press it flat, tuck the gap edges in, and topstitch close to the edge.
days.task: Make a small flat item (a placemat or cushion cover) with the turn-through method.
days.challenge: Make the same item in a second fabric without looking at the video.

quiz.q: What is the simple turn-through technique?
options: Sewing two pieces right sides together, leaving a gap, then turning them out
quiz.explain: You sew around the edge, leave a gap, turn the piece right side out and topstitch it closed.

quiz.q: Why leave a gap when you sew around the piece?
options: So you can turn the fabric right side out through it
quiz.explain: The gap is the opening you pull the fabric through to turn it the right way round.

quiz.q: What should you do after turning the piece right side out?
options: Press it flat and topstitch around the edge
quiz.explain: Pressing flat and topstitching closes the gap and gives a neat, strong edge.

video.title: One Simple Technique = Countless Easy Sewing Projects | Beginner Friendly

steps: Try a garment on inside out and pin out the excess at the side seams.
Fix a gaping neckline by taking in the shoulder seam.
Fix a tight bust by letting out the side seams.
Fix a sagging back by shortening the back waist.

days.goal: Press seams, hems and garments to a shop-quality finish.

video.title: How to Draft a Custom Fit Bodice Pattern

steps: Press every seam as you sew, never waiting until the end.
Use a pressing cloth on Ankara and delicate fabrics.
Press darts toward the centre and hems upward from the inside.
Hang the finished garment for 30 minutes before the final check.

Time yourself sewing it and value your hours at a fair rate.
Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean selling price.
Compare your price with two tailors in your area.

capstone.title: Sew a Complete Two-Piece Outfit
capstone.brief: Design, cut and sew a complete two-piece outfit (top and skirt, or a dress with a jacket) for a real wearer, fitted, pressed and presented with a costing sheet.
checks: Outfit designed and cut from your own measurements or a client's
Bodice or top fits at bust, waist and shoulders
Skirt or second piece fits and matches the top
Zip, facing and hems finished cleanly with no raw edges
Garment pressed to a shop-ready finish
Photos taken: front, back and detail
Costing sheet shows fabric, notions, time and selling price
deliverables: Finished two-piece outfit, pressed and wearable
Three photos: front, back and detail
Short care note for the wearer
